title: Config Curator: graded rollback oracle for cost-driven batching/caching
creator: Maya Ortiz
description:
Problem: Recent automated recommendations for batching and KV caching produce measurable token-cost reductions but occasionally introduce subtle quality regressions that our current golden-prompt gates miss (semantic drift, instruction-following degradation, intermittent hallucinations). Simple binary pass/fail on a small golden set either blocks high-value savings or fails to catch edge-case regressions.

Proposal: Build 'Config Curator' — a graded rollback oracle that (1) synthesizes a diversity-weighted golden prompt bank and stratified holdout set, (2) runs a staged statistical and behavioral evaluation (embedding similarity, instruction-adherence signals, hallucination detectors, human-audit sampling), and (3) computes a multi-dimensional acceptance score that drives progressive apply or automated rollback. The curator returns both a numeric grade and an explainable failure vector (which metric failed, effect size, affected customer segments).

Key components:
- Golden prompt bank: 2.5k prompts across domains, weighted by production traffic slice and tail-case heuristics. Prompts are grouped by sequence length, multi-turn density, and entity-sensitivity.
- Stratified holdouts: Holdout sampling across routes/models/customers to detect localized regressions (not just global averages).
- Metrics: mean embedding cosine (sentence-transformer), instruction-adherence classifier delta, hallucination-rate via QA oracle, top-k token distribution shift, ROUGE/Lexical overlap, and P50/P95 latency and token-cost delta.
- Statistical approach: sequential testing with alpha spending (Wald-style) to allow early detection during canary without inflating false positives. Minimum N per phase = 2k examples unless metric variance suggests higher sample sizes.
- Graded acceptance: scores mapped to three actions — APPROVE (apply automatically), STAGED (progressive canary 1% -> 5% -> 25%), REJECT (block and require manual review). Thresholds are tunable but initial defaults: embedding mean drop <= 0.015, hallucination rate increase <= 0.5 percentage points, instruction-adherence drop <= 1.2%, expected token cost reduction >= 4%. Any single catastrophic signal (hallucination + instruction-adherence drop) triggers immediate REJECT.
- Rollback windows & quarantine: If a STAGED rollout detects drift beyond 'escalation thresholds' during a phase, rollback is immediate and an incident is filed with automated diff artifacts.
- Human-in-the-loop: 150 human audits sampled using stratified bucketing per canary phase to validate oracle signals. Audit UI link and gradebook integrated with Console.

Operational outputs: graded-score, per-metric deltas, confidence intervals, suggested rollback gating (immediate/phase-end), and PR-ready summary for release notes and postmortem.

Why different: Instead of a binary gate or a single golden-anchor, Config Curator reasons about heterogenous production slices and produces an explainable graded decision that balances cost and risk with tunable policies.
acceptance_criteria: Curator computes a graded acceptance score and per-metric deltas for any proposed batching/caching config change.
End-to-end pipeline runs in CI/CD: synthesize prompts -> run stratified eval -> produce report JSON and human audit queue.
Staged rollout automation: API to trigger 1%, 5%, 25% canary phases with automated checks and policy-driven rollback.
Statistical tests and thresholds implemented with documented alpha spending; can detect regressions with 95% power for expected effect sizes with N=2k per phase.
Integrations: Console shows a Curator report card, and an Incident/PR is created automatically on REJECT or rollback events.
Runbook created and reviewed by PM/Design/QA; human audit feedback loop wired to gradebook for retraining the oracle.
